/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 13 May 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 3189 (126)
Baltic Capesize Index: 5340 (258)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2454 (94)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1553 (18)
Baltic Handysize Index: 848 (5)
CAPESIZE
The market extended its upward trajectory today, building further on the strong momentum generated by yesterday’s particularly active afternoon out of South Brazil and West Africa into China. Both basins continued to firm, with improving sentiment supported by stronger fixing activity, tightening tonnage in key regions, and firmer bid levels emerging across the major routes. The BCI 182 5TC gained a further $2,343 to close at $48,433. C5 pushed higher by 0.715 to $15.890, while C3 posted another notable gain, jumping $1.391 to settle at $37.127. In the Pacific, conditions continued to improve steadily, with two major miners active on C5 helping underpin sentiment. Bids were reportedly starting the day in the low $15s before firming considerably, with reports circulating by close of play of $15.80 being paid, highlighting the stronger undertone developing through the session. The Atlantic also maintained a positive tone following the burst of activity seen late yesterday, where reports suggested as many as 9–10 fixtures concluded on C3 in the low $36s up to $37 range. Momentum carried into today, with reports of $37.25 being paid for 8/10 June loading further reinforcing the firmer sentiment. Conditions in the North Atlantic also remain tight, with improving front-haul bids reportedly emerging from East Coast Canada into China as owners continue to gain confidence.
PANAMAX
Today marked another active session in the Panamax market, with the positive momentum continuing. Reports from brokers suggest that trans Atlantic mineral and grain volumes remain steady, underpinned by firm market sentiment, which is driving owners’ offers further upward. Several stronger fixtures have also been concluded, reinforcing the ongoing rise in rates. Fronthaul activity remains buoyant, with elevated levels and numerous fixtures reported. Market participants continue to emphasise the strength of the North Coast South America and US East Coast regions. In the Pacific, demand for prompt tonnage persists, with brokers indicating that the shorter Indonesian runs are commanding a premium to attract vessels. Supply from Australia and the North Pacific remains healthy with multiple fixtures reported, helping to support and lift the market floor. Brokers have also noted increased period activity today, with a variety of fixtures concluded highlighting the continuing appetite from charterers. The P5TC improved today by $842 to conclude at $22,083.
SUPRAMAX
Another positional day certainly from the Atlantic, the US Gulf was finely balanced although again some maintained a ceiling had been reached. Broker said better levels of enquiry were being seen from the South Atlantic and rates pushed upward. The Continent-Mediterranean again failed to gain traction, with a good supply of prompt tonnage. The Asian arena continued it upward climb, brokers said that demand had returned from the north for both the NoPac and backhaul which helped owners’ expectations. The Desert Pioneer (60,980 2022) open Chittagong 14/19 May was heard fixed for short period at $18,000, but no more details surfaced. The 11TC average closed up $217 at $19,625.

Atlantic
The Maria (63,153 2015) open Annaba prompt was heard fixed with clinker basis delivery Djen Djen redelivery Nouackhott at $11,700, but no more details came to light.

Asia
The Beilun 17 (63,151 2014) open Far East was heard to have been fixed for a backhaul to West Africa at $23,000. A 64,000 open CJK was heard fixed for a trip East Africa at $25,000, further details were not disclosed. Elsewhere, a 61,000 open Chittagong fixed a trip China at $20,000.

HANDYSIZE
It was a mixed day for activity, with only modest shifts across both basins. The BHSI edged up 5 points to 848, while the 7TC Average settled at $15,255, an increase of $90. Activity continued to slow across the Continent and the Mediterranean with some sources described as positional but little information surfaced. In the South Atlantic, fundamentals softened and rates remained largely flat. In the US Gulf, sentiment continued to improve as tonnage tightened slightly, with rates were recorded a tick higher than last done. In Asia, the market continue to benefit from healthy cargo volumes, which led to a general uptick in activity and a slight rise in rates. The ATN Unity (30,611 2007), open Indonesia mid-May, fixed high $9,000 for multi legs, though further details were not disclosed. In addition, a 33,000 open Jakarta 15-30 May was heard fixed at $15,000 for a trip via Australia to Far East, and a 28,000open South Korea was heard fixed to SE Asia at around $13,000, with no further details available.

Market Fundamentals
South African Coal Export Strength

Customs data show South African coal exports rose 10% y-o-y in March to 7.19 Mt. Exports to Pakistan more than doubled y-o-y to 812.7 kt following the disruption of Qatari LNG exports to the country, and exports to India increased 19% y-o-y to 3.9 Mt thanks to restocking at sponge iron producers. Preliminary estimates from vessel tracking data suggest exports fell by almost 20% m-o-m in April, but were up nearly 2% y-o-y.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve rallied higher on open in reaction to yesterday’s stronger C3 fixtures, combined with a firmer Pacific market today. The biggest move was on the May and June contracts with 43000 and 39500 paid respectively. The May v Jun spread widened and strengthened late on up to a high of 4000 in good volume. July was active again trading up to 35750, before closing negative on day with offers sub 35000. The Q3 range was wide 33150-33850 and the Q4 32000-32600. Cal27 traded marginally higher up to 26850 and similarly the Cal28, with pays up to 23400.

PMX
The PMX market saw a softer day across the curve, with sellers searching for bids early on and pressure seen across the front months. May traded in a tight range of 22000–21600, while Jun was again the main point of interest, printing a high of 23550 and being paid down to 22700, finishing the day around this level. July moved lower from 22800 to 21900, with Aug holding around 20900. Q3 was another key area of focus, trading between 21750 and 20900 before closing around 21000. Q4 printed from 19100 down to 18700. Further out, Cal 27 was paid down to a low of 15450, while Cal 28 traded at 14250 and Cal 29 at 13750.

SMX + HANDY
SMX market eased from the recent highs today, as buyers appeared to take pause and the curve drifted lower as a result. May gapped down on open and traded within a narrow range between 17650 – 17850. Jun traded from 19850 to 19000, Jul 19500 – 19000 and Q3 18900 down to 18400. Cal27 once again traded a few times, with the individual quarters also garnering some interest, Q1’27 changed hands between 12850 - 12750, Q2’27-Q4’27 strip also trading at 13850, while Cal27 traded 13725 – 13675 and Cal28 at 12575.

Market Fundamentals
South African Coal Export Strength
Customs data show South African coal exports rose 10% y-o-
y in March to 7.19 Mt. Exports to Pakistan more than
doubled y-o-y to 812.7 kt following the disruption of Qatari
LNG exports to the country, and exports to India increased
19% y-o-y to 3.9 Mt thanks to restocking at sponge iron
producers. Preliminary estimates from vessel tracking data
suggest exports fell by almost 20% m-o-m in April, but were
up nearly 2% y-o-y.
Trading Commentary
Cape Routes
Markets along the routes were quiet and largely inactive
today, with minimal trading reported. The only trade was the
C5 June contract at 14.60 early in the session, where it later
closed valued. There was some interest in the Jun vs Jul
spread again, but no deals were concluded. The C3 June
contract declined slightly, closing valued at 35.00. Overall,
the rest of the curve remained thin with very limited liquidity
and activity.
Cape
The Cape FFA curve rallied higher on open in reaction to
yesterday’s stronger C3 ﬁxtures, combined with a ﬁrmer
Paciﬁc market today. The biggest move was on the May and
June contracts with 43000 and 39500 paid respectively. The
May v Jun spread widened and strengthened late on up to a
high of 4000 in good volume. July was active again trading
up to 35750, before closing negative on day with oﬀers sub
35000. The Q3 range was wide 33150-33850 and the Q4
32000-32600. Cal27 traded marginally higher up to 26850
and similarly the Cal28, with pays up to 23400.
PMX
The PMX market saw a softer day across the curve, with
sellers searching for bids early on and pressure seen across
the front months. May traded in a tight range of 22000–
21600, while Jun was again the main point of interest,
printing a high of 23550 and being paid down to 22700,
ﬁnishing the day around this level. July moved lower from
22800 to 21900, with Aug holding around 20900. Q3 was
another key area of focus, trading between 21750 and 20900
before closing around 21000. Q4 printed from 19100 down
to 18700. Further out, Cal 27 was paid down to a low of
15450, while Cal 28 traded at 14250 and Cal 29 at 13750.
SMX + HANDY
SMX market eased from the recent highs today, as buyers
appeared to take pause and the curve drifted lower as a
result. May gapped down on open and traded within a
narrow range between 17650 – 17850. Jun traded from
19850 to 19000, Jul 19500 – 19000 and Q3 18900 down to
18400. Cal27 once again traded a few times, with the
individual quarters also garnering some interest, Q1’27
changed hands between 12850 - 12750, Q2’27-Q4’27 strip
also trading at 13850, while Cal27 traded 13725 – 13675 and
Cal28 at 12575.Cape 180 5TC

items.parsed_text: 13th May 2026 Iron Ore TSI 62%: - - TSI Premium Coking Coal: - - Brent UK Oil: 107.93 0.16 EUA: - - BDI 3,189 126 BCI 180 5,340 258 BPI 2,454 94 BSI 1,553 18 BHSI 848 5 Market Fundamentals South African Coal Export Strength Customs data show South African coal exports rose 10% y-o- y in March to 7.19 Mt. Exports to Pakistan more than doubled y-o-y to 812.7 kt following the disruption of Qatari LNG exports to the country, and exports to India increased 19% y-o-y to 3.9 Mt thanks to restocking at sponge iron producers. Preliminary estimates from vessel tracking data suggest exports fell by almost 20% m-o-m in April, but were up nearly 2% y-o-y. Trading Commentary Cape Routes Markets along the routes were quiet and largely inactive today, with minimal trading reported. The only trade was the C5 June contract at 14.60 early in the session, where it later closed valued. There was some interest in the Jun vs Jul spread again, but no deals were concluded. The C3 June contract declined slightly, closing valued at 35.00. Overall, the rest of the curve remained thin with very limited liquidity and activity. Cape The Cape FFA curve rallied higher on open in reaction to yesterday’s stronger C3 fixtures, combined with a firmer Pacific market today. The biggest move was on the May and June contracts with 43000 and 39500 paid respectively. The May v Jun spread widened and strengthened late on up to a high of 4000 in good volume. July was active again trading up to 35750, before closing negative on day with offers sub 35000. The Q3 range was wide 33150-33850 and the Q4 32000-32600. Cal27 traded marginally higher up to 26850 and similarly the Cal28, with pays up to 23400. PMX The PMX market saw a softer day across the curve, with sellers searching for bids early on and pressure seen across the front months. May traded in a tight range of 22000– 21600, while Jun was again the main point of interest, printing a high of 23550 and being paid down to 22700, finishing the day around this level. July moved lower from 22800 to 21900, with Aug holding around 20900. Q3 was another key area of focus, trading between 21750 and 20900 before closing around 21000. Q4 printed from 19100 down to 18700. Further out, Cal 27 was paid down to a low of 15450, while Cal 28 traded at 14250 and Cal 29 at 13750. SMX + HANDY SMX market eased from the recent highs today, as buyers appeared to take pause and the curve drifted lower as a result. May gapped down on open and traded within a narrow range between 17650 – 17850. Jun traded from 19850 to 19000, Jul 19500 – 19000 and Q3 18900 down to 18400. Cal27 once again traded a few times, with the individual quarters also garnering some interest, Q1’27 changed hands between 12850 - 12750, Q2’27-Q4’27 strip also trading at 13850, while Cal27 traded
